findings.issue: The SPEC-10 browser test would still pass if the ActionBar onClick guard (`model.enabled && action !== null`) were removed. React drops onClick for a <button> whose React prop `disabled` is true, whatever the DOM attribute says. Even if it fired, the idle buttons carry action null and useTableSession.act is a no-op unless nextStep(t) === 'user'. The test checks the end-to-end behaviour SPEC-10 asks for ('changes nothing'), so it is not wrong. But it does not protect the guard. SPEC-11 is the test that fails without the guard.
findings.evidence: node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.production.js:1686-1712 getListener returns no onClick listener when props.disabled is true for button/input/select/textarea; src/ui/table/useTableSession.ts:112-114 act ignores actions unless nextStep(t)==='user'.
findings.fix: Change nothing in the code. Optionally add a comment in the test saying the guard itself is covered by SPEC-11 (tests/ui/action-bar-limits.acceptance.test.tsx), and don't describe this e2e test as a guard test in the story doc.

findings.issue: SPEC-11 calls onClick on idle buttons, and every idle button has action null. So it catches removal of the whole guard, but not removal of the `model.enabled` half alone.
findings.fix: Optionally also call onClick on ActionBar({ model: { enabled: false, buttons: [{ label: 'Call $4', action: { seat: 5, type: 'call', amount: 4 } }] }, onAct: spy }) and expect spy not called.

summary: The implementation matches the spec. fullBetTarget is a pure extraction: legalActions computes the same min(fullBetLevel+betUnit, maxTo), and the only other change is the parameter types. isShortAllIn uses strict '<', so a stack that exactly covers the call, bet or raise keeps the plain label (A-1), and that is tested for call, bet and raise (SPEC-03, SPEC-13). It handles preflop through the big-blind level in fullBetLevel. A non-reopening short raise (TASK-1.14) is ignored by the full target (SPEC-07, SPEC-13 assert fullBetTarget = 8 after the $5 short raise). Chip labels print plain digits with no $ and no separator. The SPEC-08 oracle does not use isShortAllIn or actionLabel: it re-runs legalActions with the actor's stack at 1e9 and has its own formatter. It is not vacuous: it asserts exactly 100,000 decisions, all sizes 2-10, capped > 0, non-reopened > 0, and each all-in, chip and dollar label class. It catches table-layer bugs ('<=' or stack==0 as 'all-in'), but not a wrong engine fullBetTarget, because both sides use legalActions; that is acceptable since the bar must mirror the engine. The TASK-3.2 locked files are untouched by this branch. All five relevant vitest files pass locally (100k property ~1 s). There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. The stripped-disabled e2e test would not fail if the click guard were removed (React suppresses onClick on disabled-prop buttons); SPEC-11 covers the guard.
